text: The Conclave Laboratory remembers your summer, and especially the ward that held. Your old supervisor writes that a place as a junior researcher is yours from the autumn if you'll take it. "Don't make me ask twice," she adds. Answer by the last day.

The Guild of Alchemists' works remember your summer and the batch you saved. The foreman writes, in a hand that has clearly been burned more than once, that a journeyman's bench is yours from the autumn. Answer by the last day.

A blank page, until you hold it to the candle. The Office of Unseen Affairs remembers your summer, and the file you didn't open. A desk is yours from the autumn. No reply is needed; they will know your answer on the last day.

The Beastcraft Field Station remembers your summer on the moors. The warden writes that a keeper's post is yours from the autumn, with a cottage, a lamp and more creatures than any sane person would count. Answer by the last day.

say: You leave the line about the Ledger's special edition. The editor looks relieved; it was her favourite. You strike out every line. The editor sighs and prints your name and the year, and nothing else. It suits you, somehow.

text: The photographer is herding the year onto the great hall steps. At the end of a row, two pale heads lean together, Kael and Ilse, who was raised to open the door he refused. Kael sees you and moves up, which leaves a space between them and the edge.

You cut through the first-years' lecture on your way somewhere else. In the front row, alone, sits a first-year with red ink on her fingers. The lecturer asks her a question. She opens her mouth, and nothing comes out, and the hall waits until she looks at the floor. The robes are the ones from the stair, two sizes too big.

story.name: Red ink
story.premise: Someone unsigned keeps marking your essays in red, and they're right.

entries.text: Someone marked your essay in red ink, unsigned, and was right. You rewrote it and left it on the stair.
The red ink is hers: a first-year who can't say a word in front of a room. She has a seminar on Thursday.
On Thursday she spoke, all the way to the end.

text: Corvin deals you a hand from an old deck, soft at the corners and smelling of pipe smoke. "Grandfather's," he says. "It really is lucky. Watch." You win, which shouldn't be possible against Corvin.
